 Qantas to cut 850 jobs in Accenture AI outsourcing deal, Greens say
 Qantas will cut 850 jobs after outsourcing work to Accenture, with hundreds of roles going offshore in an AI overhaul, the Australian Greens say. Greens workplace spokesperson Barbara Pocock said Labor was “doing nothing to protect workers from AI-driven job cuts”. 
 Published 20 November 2026 
 2 min read 
 Share this story Share LinkedIn WhatsApp Teams Facebook X Copy link Qantas will cut 850 jobs under a deal to outsource work to consultancy firm Accenture, the Australian Greens said in a statement on 11 November 2026. According to the Greens, hundreds of the roles will be moved offshore as part of an AI overhaul.
 The Greens noted that the announcement comes after reports that Telstra and Coles have also shed hundreds of jobs following their own arrangements with Accenture.
 The Greens set the job losses against the airline’s finances. According to the party, Qantas recorded a statutory after-tax profit of $1.29 billion in the last financial year, while its chief executive received $6.8 million over the same period. The party also pointed to the $2.7 billion in public funding the airline received during the peak of the pandemic, “in part to keep its workers employed”.
 Senator Barbara Pocock, the Greens spokesperson for finance, workplace and employment and a Senator for South Australia, said: “Big corporations are hiding behind claims of cost savings while raking in massive profits. It’s a pathetic excuse for slashing jobs.”
 She also criticised Labor. “Workers are paying the price while the corporate giants cash in and Labor is doing nothing to protect workers from AI-driven job cuts,” she said. “Where is Labor, the so -called ‘party for workers’? Too busy signing contracts with Accenture.”
 Senator Pocock also pointed to the Bureau of Meteorology website project, on which Accenture and Deloitte secured contract extensions. “What started as a $4 million project ballooned to $96 million,” she said, adding that consultancy firms had used contract amendments “to milk government contracts for more money”.
 “We cannot allow corporations to use AI to undermine workers’ skills, destroy jobs and drive down conditions. Workers’ rights and job security must come first.” Senator Barbara Pocock, Australian Greens
 Senator Pocock also addressed how the gains from new technology are shared. “Working Australians deserve a fair share of the productivity gains from AI and new technology, not more job insecurity while billionaires and big corporations pocket the profits and wages fall behind,” she said.
